newsitem.title: USA: Western U.S. labor markets tighten - report.
newsitem.headline: Western U.S. labor markets tighten - report.

text.p: Labor markets in the western United States have tightened as the region continues to lead the nation in economic growth, according to a Bank of America report released on Tuesday.
Total nonfarm payroll employment in the region grew 3.4 percent from February 1996 to February 1997, Bank of America's regional economist Howard Roth said in the report.

Arizona, Nevada and Utah were the top three states in the nation in job growth, he said. Oregon and Washington also were among the top 10 states, while Colorado, Idaho and California were among the top 15, the report said.
Gains in total personal income have strengthened from a year earlier and remain stronger than gains in the other three major regional economies, the report said.

For the three months to February 1997, issuance of residential building permits in the West was down almost 9.0 percent from a year earlier. For most western states, this represented a leveling off from high levels of residential construction, the report said.
The report, titled "Economic & Business Outlook -- 1997 Regional Outlook," was produced by the Economics and Policy Research Department at Bank of America, a unit of BankAmerica Corp.
